blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Taxes can sound difficult, but in English they follow simple patterns. Today's lesson is about simple tax calculation. You will learn a few useful words and practise them in short sentences.

Taxes are just one more part of the company's routine. At Czarnikow, the fiscal team checks the numbers before every deadline. They read the forms slowly and make sure everything is correct.

English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts. Go slowly — one small step at a time. Learn five words today and practise in easy sentences. You can do it!

items.q: What is today's lesson about?
items.why: "Today's lesson is about simple tax calculation."

items.q: According to the text, taxes are…
options: one more part of the company's routine
items.why: "Taxes are just one more part of the company's routine."

items.q: When does the fiscal team check the numbers?
items.why: "the fiscal team checks the numbers before every deadline."

items.q: The phrase "one small step at a time" suggests that you should…
items.why: Inferência: "Go slowly — one small step at a time" pede paciência, um passo de cada vez.

items.q: The author would most likely AGREE that…
options: you can learn English step by step
items.why: Inferência: "English comes in CAN's… You can do it!" — o texto é positivo e encorajador.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie comparar os impostos de dois países com o aluno. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi! I'm Sophie. Today let's compare taxes in two countries. It is easy with simple words. Look at Country A and Country B.

In Country A, the tax is high. In Country B, the tax is low. So the tax in Country A is higher than the tax in Country B. And the tax in Country B is lower than in Country A. Very simple, right?

Now look at the numbers on the form. Country A has a big number. Country B has a small number. The number in Country A is bigger than in Country B. The number in Country B is smaller than in Country A.

Do you see the pattern? We use the word "than" to compare two things. Higher than. Lower than. Bigger than. Smaller than. It is always the same. One small step at a time.

Remember: the high number must be correct before we send the form. Our fiscal team checks every small number before the deadline. Take it slow, and practise a little every day. You can do it! Are you ready for the next tax word?
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Sophie compare in this audio?
items.why: "Today let's compare taxes in two countries."

items.q: The tax in Country A is…
items.why: "the tax in Country A is higher than the tax in Country B."

items.q: The number in Country B is…
items.why: "The number in Country B is smaller."

items.q: Which word does Sophie use to compare?
items.why: Inferência: ela repete "higher than, lower than, bigger than, smaller than" — a palavra-chave para comparar é "than".

items.q: How would you best describe Sophie's tone?
items.why: Inferência: "Take it slow. You can do it!" — ela é calma e encorajadora.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The tax in this country is very high." High means…
items.why: High = alto.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The tax in Country B is ___, so we pay less."
items.why: Low = baixo; se pagamos menos, o imposto é baixo.

items.q: "Country A has a big number on the form." Big means…
items.why: Big = grande.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We check every ___ number before the deadline."
items.why: Small = pequeno; checamos cada número pequeno também.

items.q: "The tax is higher than last year." Than means…
items.why: Than = do que; usamos para comparar (higher than = mais alto do que).

blocks.instruction: Expressões simples que aparecem no trabalho com impostos. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager must sign off on the tax form." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar, dar o "ok" final.

items.q: "We will roll out the new tax form next month." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = colocar em uso, lançar.

items.q: "Please fill in the tax form." To fill in means to…
items.why: Fill in = preencher (escrever as informações).

items.q: "Let's go over the numbers before the deadline." To go over means to…
items.why: Go over = revisar, checar com cuidado.

items.q: "We must hand in the form today." To hand in means to…
items.why: Hand in = entregar (enviar/submeter).
